overview: This Senate resolution supports naming April 2025 "National Child Abuse Prevention Month." It describes the long-term harm that abuse, neglect, and other traumatic childhood experiences can cause, and points to the large number of children referred to child protective services each year and the rise in reports of online child sexual exploitation. It notes that voluntary home visiting programs, in which trained workers visit families with young children, have helped reduce repeat abuse. The resolution supports public awareness and education about preventing child abuse, and supports healing and justice for survivors. It does not create programs or provide money. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on April 29, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution draws attention to a preventable harm and encourages efforts to protect children and support survivors.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or provide funding for prevention programs.
